title: InEgypt: Egypt Trip Planner, Metro & Train Routes for iPhone
description: Free iPhone app for visiting Egypt: a day-by-day trip plan, routes by metro, train and bus, and fair prices and scams to know before you pay.

hero.h1: Plan your Egypt trip. Get around with confidence.
hero.lead: Build a day-by-day plan, find the train or metro between your stops, and check what things cost before you pay.
hero.underBadge: Free on iPhone and iPad · No account needed · 9 languages
hero.photoAlt: The Giza pyramids under a red evening sky.
hero.screenAlt: An InEgypt trip from Luxor to Aswan on the map, with the day's visits and the travel time between them.

price.title: What should the ride into Cairo cost?
price.body: Before you agree on a fare, check the range for a taxi into the city. InEgypt also explains common airport scams and keeps emergency numbers close at hand.
price.others: More fair prices, each with the date it was checked

train.title: How do I get from Cairo to Luxor?
train.body: Your plan includes the ride between cities. Compare departures, journey times and stops in the published timetable. For the rest of the trip, the same search covers the metro, tram, monorail, LRT, BRT, coaches and domestic flights.
train.alt: The Cairo to Luxor timetable in InEgypt, showing departure and arrival times for two trains.
train.modesLabel: Ways to travel in one search
train.honest: Times come from published timetables. Local buses in Cairo and Alexandria are a fallback and less complete.

maker.title: Made in Egypt, by one developer.
maker.note: I started InEgypt as a guide to places. Metro and train routes came next. Today, it brings those routes into the plan for your day. I still answer the support mail myself.

review.text: It's very helpful and full of information about what to visit in each city, saved me time to plan for my next trip.

more.text: The best app for traveling in Egypt
…well designed and easy to use. As Egyptian.. it adds to me .. so I think it will be very useful to travelers and visitors..

install.title: Take InEgypt with you.
install.free: Free to download, with no account. Plan your days, check prices and search routes; your saved trip and emergency numbers open offline.

iphone.title: Made for iPhone
items: Siri and Shortcuts: “Ask InEgypt for directions”
iPhone and iPad, iOS 18 or later

items.a: Yes. Routes, places, the price guide and trip planning are free. Offline routes, extra automatic plans, trip weather and expenses are paid.
Partly. A saved trip, place pages and the emergency page open offline for free. Offline route search is paid.
No. InEgypt is for iPhone and iPad (iOS 18 or later).

items.q: Which cities and transport does it cover?
items.a: InEgypt plans across metro, train, monorail, BRT, LRT, tram, intercity coaches and domestic flights. Cairo and Alexandria local buses are included as a helpful fallback: useful, but not as complete or current as the rail lines. It covers {cities} cities and {attractions} attractions.

items.q: Can I buy train or attraction tickets in the app?
items.a: No. InEgypt links to the official sellers.

items.q: Does it show live arrival times?
items.a: No. Times come from published timetables.

items.q: Can I use it before I arrive?
items.a: Yes. Plan the trip at home and it is ready when you land.

items.q: I already have an itinerary from ChatGPT. Can I use it?
items.a: Yes. Paste it; InEgypt finds the places, orders the days and shows the travel time. This is free.
Ahmed Elawady, an independent developer in Egypt, has made InEgypt since 2020.

plan.title: Your whole trip, planned day by day.
plan.body: Pick your dates and cities, or paste a plan you already made. InEgypt puts the days in a sensible order, adds real travel time between stops and tells you when a day does not fit.
plan.photoAlt: Rows of carved columns at Karnak in Luxor.
plan.screenAlt: A Luxor itinerary with a visit to the Valley of the Kings, the taxi ride and dinner that follows.
plan.caption: Karnak, Luxor
steps: Dates, cities and what you enjoy, or let InEgypt suggest how long to stay.
Visits, meals and the travel time between them, so you see how full each day is.
A warning when a day does not fit
Move a visit or add a day while you are still at home.

strip.caption: Cities in one trip are joined by real transport, for example the sleeper train to Luxor.

paste.title: Already have a plan?
paste.text: Paste one from ChatGPT, a blog or your notes. InEgypt finds the places, orders the days and adds the travel time. Free.

discover.body: Every place page has opening notes, what to know before you go and a button to add it to your trip. Where an official ticket seller exists, InEgypt links to it.

safety.title: And if something goes wrong?
safety.body: Tourist police, ambulance and the other emergency numbers are one tap away, and the emergency page opens without internet. Next to them: what to do about airport taxi touts, the “ticket office is closed” line and other common tricks.
safety.emergencyAlt: The emergency page in InEgypt: general emergency, police, ambulance, fire, tourist police and more, each with a call button.
safety.tipsAlt: Safety tips in InEgypt, from airport taxi touts to uninvited porters.
